quick: Oral: 500 mg three times daily; topical 2% applied 2-3 times daily
Take oral tablets with or after food
Caution / avoid in significant impairment - hepatobiliary excretion
summary: Fusidic acid is a narrow-spectrum steroidal (fusidane) antibiotic with strong activity against Gram-positive bacteria, especially Staphylococcus aureus including many MRSA strains. It is used topically for staphylococcal skin and eye infections and systemically (often as sodium fusidate, usually combined with another anti-staphylococcal agent to prevent resistance) for deep staphylococcal infections such as osteomyelitis. It is not FDA-approved.
indications: Topical treatment of primary and secondary staphylococcal skin infections (e.g., impetigo, infected dermatoses)
Topical (eye drops) treatment of staphylococcal conjunctivitis / blepharitis
Systemic treatment of staphylococcal infections including osteomyelitis, skin and soft tissue, and endocarditis (in combination)

dosage.d: 500 mg three times daily (suspension dosing is higher)
dosage.n: Use in combination with another antistaphylococcal antibiotic to limit resistance

dosage.d: Apply a thin layer to the affected area 2-3 times daily
dosage.t: 2-3 times daily, usually up to 7 days
dosage.n: Avoid prolonged use to limit resistance

dosage.d: One drop into the affected eye(s) twice daily
dosage.n: Continue for 48 hours after the eye is normal

admin: Take oral tablets/suspension with or after food
Apply topical preparations thinly to the affected area after cleaning
For eye drops, instill into the conjunctival sac and avoid touching the dropper to the eye
Complete the prescribed systemic course; do not use systemic fusidic acid as monotherapy
moa: Fusidic acid inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding to elongation factor G (EF-G) and preventing its dissociation from the ribosome, thereby blocking translocation during translation. It is primarily bacteriostatic but bactericidal at higher concentrations and is especially active against staphylococci.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to fusidic acid or sodium fusidate
Concomitant systemic use with statins (e.g., simvastatin, atorvastatin) - risk of rhabdomyolysis

preg: Systemic fusidic acid should be used in pregnancy only if clearly needed; topical and ophthalmic use carries minimal systemic exposure. There are no adequate controlled human studies.
lact: Small amounts may pass into breast milk with systemic use; use systemic therapy with caution. Topical and ophthalmic use is considered low risk; avoid application to the breast while nursing.
renal: No dose adjustment is generally required in renal impairment because fusidic acid is eliminated mainly via the bile rather than the kidneys.
hepatic: Use with caution and monitor liver function in hepatic impairment, as fusidic acid undergoes hepatobiliary metabolism and excretion and can cause cholestatic jaundice; avoid in significant impairment.

major: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors (statins) - markedly increased statin levels and rhabdomyolysis (avoid combination with systemic fusidic acid)
HIV protease inhibitors / certain antiretrovirals (mutual increase in levels)
moderate: Other hepatically metabolised drugs (competition for excretion)
minor: Other topical antibacterials (avoid concurrent use to limit resistance)
interactions.food: Take oral doses with food to improve tolerability
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor liver function tests with systemic use; may cause transient hyperbilirubinaemia

common: Topical: local irritation, stinging, rash, contact dermatitis
rare: Blood dyscrasias (thrombocytopenia, neutropenia) with prolonged systemic use

monitoring: Liver function tests during systemic therapy
Clinical response and emergence of resistance
Muscle symptoms / creatine kinase if a statin was recently co-administered
counsel: Complete the full course as prescribed; do not stop early
For systemic therapy, tell your doctor about statins - the combination can cause serious muscle damage
Use topical preparations only for the prescribed duration to avoid resistance
Report yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, or unexplained muscle pain
For eye drops, do not touch the dropper to the eye and remove contact lenses
pk: Antibacterial effect over the dosing course
Supports systemic dosing two to three times daily
Store below 25-30 C; do not freeze eye drops; protect from light
pearls: Excellent anti-staphylococcal activity (including many MRSA) - reserve and combine systemically to prevent resistance
Do not co-prescribe systemic fusidic acid with statins - risk of rhabdomyolysis
Eliminated mainly via bile, so renal impairment rarely needs dose change; watch the liver instead
missed: Take or apply the missed dose as soon as remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose, in which case skip it and resume the usual schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Topical and ophthalmic overdose is unlikely to cause systemic toxicity. Systemic overdose may cause gastrointestinal upset and hepatic disturbance; management is supportive with monitoring of liver function. There is no specific antidote.
